assignments.note: 2025-05 Which Agent Causes Task Failures and When
assignments.why: The Who&When dataset of labelled multi-agent failure logs is an agent benchmark with step-level scoring; the three LLM attribution methods judge trajectories to find the failing agent and step.
Its subject is a multi-agent judge that assesses business documents for accuracy, consistency, completeness and clarity.

assignments.note: 2025-06 AI debate aids assessment of controversial claims
assignments.why: Debate is the evaluation method under test, and the act of judging by human and AI judges with prior beliefs is the subject.
A new recursive debate protocol for evaluation that lets the honest debater win against obfuscation.

assignments.note: 2025-06 CURE Co-Evolving Coder and Unit Tester
assignments.why: The unit tester is RL-trained to generate tests that learn from the coder's mistakes, and the trained models serve as reward models.
A benchmark of 130 agentic-search tasks, scored by task-specific judge agents with rubric trees, an extractor and a verifier.
A meta-evaluation benchmark of reward models and LLM judges, measuring their accuracy and how well it carries to downstream best-of-N and PPO.
Measures the robustness of 13 judges against 15 attacks and 8 defences; the measurement is the contribution.

assignments.note: 2025-06 Spurious rewards rethinking training signals in RLVR
assignments.why: It studies how random or wrong RLVR rewards still improve a policy; no registry topic covers the reward signal's effect on policy training (see proposal). | main session: assigned to the new topic 'judges as reward signals' created from this proposal.
Contamination probes showing SWE-bench scores reflect memorisation, a validity failure of an agent benchmark.
Exposes SWE-bench verifier failures (wrong patches passing) and fixes them with LLM-generated test augmentation.
A conversational agent benchmark whose dual-control setup centres on a simulated user who has its own tools and state.
Brier-score reward training makes the model's stated confidence calibrated, with a proper-scoring-rule theorem and ECE results in and out of domain.

assignments.note: 2025-07 Establishing Best Practices for Building Rigorous Agentic Benchmarks
assignments.why: The ABC checklist audits task and outcome validity of agent benchmarks, including verifier failures.
An agent-as-a-judge that scores financial research reports via an extracted logic tree, packaged as a 70-question benchmark for research agents.
The judge is a panel of evaluator-persona agents, and they reach scores by debating.
Measures master-key false positives across generative reward models and judges, then trains Master-RM with adversarial negatives.
Per-prompt rubrics are scored by an LLM judge to produce the reward, and the paper compares this judge design with Likert judging.
Scalar Bradley-Terry reward models trained on 26M curated preference pairs.
A gym environment for agents where simulated users reveal underspecified, evolving preferences a little at a time.
A meta-agent generates adversarial tests whose difficulty adapts to judge feedback to target weak capabilities, delivered through persona-driven simulated dialogues.
A judge agent that decomposes the task and validates each step of the actor's trajectory, which is trajectory and step-level agent scoring.
Takes multi-agent debate apart and finds that plain majority voting, an aggregation rule over agents' answers, explains most of its gains.

assignments.note: 2025-08 Dropping just a handful of preferences can change top LLM rankings
assignments.why: A sensitivity analysis of arena-style rankings built from Bradley-Terry fits to pairwise votes.
Measures judge overconfidence (ECE, the TH-Score metric) and proposes LLM-as-a-Fuser, a judge that combines several judges' verdicts, compared against voting and weighted-voting aggregation.
A review of agent-as-a-judge designs, from single-model judges to multi-agent debate.

assignments.note: 2025-09 Analyzing uncertainty of LLM-as-a-judge conformal prediction
assignments.why: Replaces a judge's point scores with conformal prediction intervals, a post-hoc method that gives its uncertainty valid coverage.
A systematic measurement of thinking versus non-thinking small judges on accuracy, cost and bias robustness, a choice of judge design.
Measures judges changing verdicts on injected provenance and recency labels when the content is the same, without saying so.
A standardised harness and leaderboard running 9 agent benchmarks, with cost tracking and log inspection.

proposals.note: 2025-06 Spurious rewards rethinking training signals in RLVR
proposals.name: reward signals in RL training
proposals.definition: How the reward that trains a policy (verifiable rewards, judge or rubric rewards, noisy, random or spurious rewards) shapes what the policy learns, and when the reward signal is or is not what drives the gain.
proposals.why_none_fit: trained judges and reward models covers training the judge or reward model, not what a given reward does to the policy, and no reward model is trained here; judge and decision-model audits measures judges, not policy training; LLM and agent judges needs a judge as subject; alternative evaluation paradigms is about ways to evaluate; calibration and the other mechanisms do not apply; preference learning needs pairwise or binary human feedback, and RLVR rewards are not that.
